text:
luis: OK team, extremely important research question for today's snack break — quick poll: which editor would survive the office potluck apocalypse?
Options:
1) Vim - fast, minimal, ruthless
2) VS Code - adaptable, brings a power strip and an extension for every casserole
3) Emacs - brings a folding table and a 200-line makefile for the potato salad
4) Other (specify)

dana: 2) VS Code. it brings snacks and an extension that labels all dishes for allergies :label: 

harper: 1) Vim. it sidles up, grabs leftovers, and disappears into the night like a raccoon :raccoon:

kyle: 3) Emacs. will take apart a slow-roasted lamb and write a minor-mode to track portions :ram:

zara: D) Sublime + a mysterious container of cookies that somehow never runs out :cookie:

luis: tally so far - Vim:1, VS Code:1, Emacs:1, Other:1

poll-bot: Poll closed automatically after 12m. Results archived in #random-archives.

dana: follow-up: which editor would host the best potluck playlist?
harper: Vim hosts vinyl only, curated silence between tracks.
kyle: Emacs hosts a 3-hour ambient set with sporadic applause.
zara: VS Code playlists are algorithmically optimized for maximum eating throughput.

luis: GIF: https://giphy.com/gifs/party-snacks-3o6Zt6ML6BklcajjsA

dana: note to self: bring utensils tomorrow. also @kyle if you bring lamb, i'll swap you my secret lemon drizzle recipe :wink:
luis: meeting note: this poll is binding. if VS Code wins we'll ask IT for an extra power strip at the snack table :powerplug:

poll-bot: Reminder: free lunch tomorrow in kitchen. RSVP in #lunch-plans.

luis: thanks everyone. scientific outcomes recorded. end of thread.
